mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Canada's accession in force January 11, 2024; apostille issued by home jurisdiction Designated Competent Authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified true copies of passport and proof of residential address for each director, officer, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or licensed lawyer in the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, and authorized signatories against FINTRAC politically exposed person definitions, the Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Sanctions List (Special Economic Measures Act), United Nations Act regulations, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Sergei Magnitsky Law), OFAC SDN List for USD-based rails, and UK/UN/EU watchlists; ongoing transaction monitoring of retainer ACH and wire payment rails under PCMLTFA Part 1 compliance obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) via the Alberta Corporate Registry System (CORES) and authorized NUANS service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be in English, French, or a transliteration of another language into Latin script; name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element (optional), and a legal element such as Inc., Corp., Ltd., Incorporated, Corporation, or Limited; non-Latin alphabet names must be transliterated for NUANS search; inclusion of 'Canada' requires Global Affairs Canada consent; inclusion of 'Alberta' requires provincial authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon NUANS name rejection: (1) obtain written reasons from the Corporate Registry; (2) file a fresh NUANS search with a revised distinctive element within the 90-day reservation window; (3) submit a formal reconsideration request to the Registrar of Corporations under section 10 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) within 30 days of the refusal, including evidence of distinctiveness and supporting submissions; (4) request an oral hearing before the Registrar if the reconsideration is denied; (5) alternatively, incorporate under a numbered company and subsequently apply for a name change once an approved name is secured.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the registered office only where a licensed corporate registered agent maintains a physical street address in Alberta and posts office boxes are prohibited. A pure virtual mail-forwarding address is insufficient for commercial substance; an overseas PR agency billing via ACH and wire retainers must maintain operational substance (books and records in Canada, responsible personnel, and client-facing infrastructure) to mitigate Canada Revenue Agency permanent establishment audit risk and non-resident residency challenges.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for Alberta Corporate Registry (estimated below 5% per annum for non-licensed industries); moderate for Canada Revenue Agency (estimated 10-15% audit probability over a five-year horizon for a non-resident-owned corporation conducting cross-border PR services with significant retainer-based revenue); banks may conduct remote or physical KYC site visits at the registered office during account onboarding.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9 (ABCA); ss. 8-21 (incorporation, articles and certificate of incorporation), s. 12 (incorporation by one or more incorporators), s. 15 (articles of incorporation), s. 17 (issuance of certificate of incorporation), s. 18 (registered office), s. 20 (directors), s. 101 (by-laws). Federal alternative: Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, with extra-provincial registration in Alberta.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registry Services Division); online filing through RegistryX and Authorized Service Providers
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed under section 15(1) of the ABCA, accompanied by a completed Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors (Form 2) where required
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is mandated under the ABCA for a business corporation; shares may be issued for nominal or non-par consideration without an escrow or capital deposit requirement. A corporation must maintain records of issued share capital but no statutory escrow account is required for a non-licenced public relations services company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator's share subscription is accepted and the shares are allotted, issued and paid as fully paid, non-assessable shares. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation is fixed at the Alberta address stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and the corporate registry is directed to keep records accordingly. RESOLVED, that the named individuals are appointed as President, Secretary and Treasurer, holding office until the next annual meeting or earlier succession. RESOLVED, that the by-laws, corporate seal and banking resolutions are adopted, and the officers are authorized to execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Report Acquisition
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry via authorized NUANS service providers; online portal: Corporate Registry (RegistryX)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name to an authorized NUANS search provider or the Alberta Corporate Registry online portal. Verify the name is distinctive and includes a prescribed legal element (e.g., 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.'). Obtain a dated NUANS search report valid for 90 days. Using an identified number name is an acceptable fallback and requires no NUANS search.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (up to three alternatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected or a conflict is identified, file a fresh NUANS report with a revised name, or proceed with an identified-number corporation name assigned by the Alberta Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta); filing via RegistryX online or by mail through an authorized service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) under the ABCA, setting out the corporate name, registered office location in Alberta, share structure and classes, restrictions on share transfers, number and identity of the first directors, and any restrictions on business activities. Sign the articles as incorporator and file with the Corporate Registry; pay the required filing fee by credit card (online) or certified cheque (paper). Electronic filers receive an immediate transaction receipt; a Certificate of Incorporation is issued once the articles are validated.
required_dossiers: Form 1 Articles of Incorporation duly signed by incorporator
Consent of the registered office (Form 2 or registered office address consent)
Notice of Directors and their consents (Form 2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'Notice of Intention to Reject' or queries the articles, respond through RegistryX or the adjudicating officer with amendments or supplementary information within the specified period; pay any applicable amendment fee and resubmit the corrected articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Number and Tax Account Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online portal; mail or telephone business window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, register the corporation with the CRA to obtain a Business Number (BN), including tax accounts for corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll (RM), and import/export where applicable. Use the 'Business Registration Online' service with the corporation's legal name, incorporation number, registered office, and director information. This step is essential for opening bank accounts and invoicing clients.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and director details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or queries the BN application, resolve discrepancies in the legal name or registered office data, call the CRA Business Window, and re-submit the registration using the certificate number and articles reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Corporate Governance Kit and Organizational Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation; corporate counsel or registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a first meeting of the board and adopt the pro-forma organizational resolution approving share subscriptions, the registered office, by-laws, officers, corporate seal, banking resolutions, and the execution of agreements. Issue share certificates, open a securities register, and prepare the corporate minute book exceeding ABCA record-keeping requirements.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent and minute book
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a governance or documentation defect is identified, pass a curative board resolution or unanimous shareholder consent recording ratification of all prior acts; re-execute deficient documents under corporate seal and file corrected notices with the Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence, Occupational Health and Safety, and Workers' Compensation Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary Business Licence Office or City of Edmonton Licensing Office; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS); Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta (WCB-Alberta)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal general business licence at the physical office location in Alberta, submitting the Certificate of Incorporation and lease evidence. Ensure compliance with the Alberta Fire Code for occupancy, obtain a building occupancy permit if required, complete OHS hazard assessments, and register with WCB-Alberta for workers' compensation coverage if employees are engaged.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of premises
Building occupancy permit / fire safety inspection report
WCB-Alberta registration form and employer declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal licensing is denied due to zoning or fire compliance matters, apply for a variance or conditional use permit, remedy identified fire safety deficiencies, and resubmit; for OHS or WCB coverage issues, submit corrective workplace documentation and comply with any supervisory inspection orders.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No Alberta industry-specific licensing board applies to public relations and media communications services under ISIC 7310; municipal business licensing authorities (e.g., City of Calgary, City of Edmonton) exercise general regulatory authority over physical premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial operating or manufacturing permit is required; a 'Municipal General Business Licence' may be required for any physical office, production studio, or event-support premises within Alberta.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) and, where federal matters arise, Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – office-based public relations and communications services are not a designated activity under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA); no Environmental Impact Assessment registration is required, except in the exceptional case of generating hazardous waste above applicable thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered for routine office operations; wastewater must be discharged to municipal sanitary sewers under local by-laws; volatile organic compound emissions from printing or signage operations must not create off-site nuisance odours; any hazardous waste, including electronic waste from office equipment, must be handled through an approved waste carrier and documented under applicable EPEA waste management controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required under the Alberta Fire Code, including a municipal inspection for means of egress, extinguishers, and emergency lighting; a building occupancy permit or leasehold improvement clearance may be required by the municipality; workplace health and safety compliance is mandated under the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Act and Code, including hazard assessments and training; Workers' Compensation Board – Alberta registration is mandatory once employee wages are paid; structural load inspection is only required for signage, mezzanines, or substantial office alterations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; the CRA is also the authority responsible for administering Alberta's collection of federal and provincial corporate income tax under the Alberta Corporate Tax Collection Agreement. Primary registration portal: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO), and taxpayer self-service portal: CRA My Business Account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Alberta business corporation: (1) incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) through Corporations Canada or the Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES), obtaining a certificate of incorporation; (2) register with the CRA for the statutory Business Number (BN) and applicable program accounts using Form RC1, either online through Business Registration Online or by mail; the CRA will issue a 15-digit BN, with the RT account identifier used for GST/HST obligations; (3) where the corporation carries on business in Alberta, complete any applicable extra-provincial registration obligations and appoint a registered office and service address under Alberta law; (4) for non-resident shareholders, no minimum local ownership is required, but directors, residence and annual return requirements must be verified under the applicable corporate statute. A BN and GST/HST account are usually issued immediately for online registration, with the effective GST/HST registration date set according to the first taxable supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the corporation is a separate legal and taxable taxpayer under the Income Tax Act, is not eligible for pass-through treatment, and there is no check-the-box election for Canadian business corporations. Resident Canadian corporations are taxable on worldwide income, while a non-resident corporation is taxable only on Canadian-source business income, employment income, certain Canadian-source investment income, and gains from dispositions of taxable Canadian property. Alberta has no general tax-exempt zone for this commercial scope, and the federal GST/HST applies at the entity level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election. Relevant statutory elections include: (i) a functional currency election under subsection 261(1) permitting eligible corporations to compute Canadian tax liabilities in a qualifying foreign currency; (ii) the section 216 election permitting a non-resident corporation to compute tax on Canadian-source rental income on a net basis as though a resident; (iii) the GST/HST election under section 156 of the Excise Tax Act for closely related registrants to treat certain inter-corporate supplies as made for no consideration and outside the scope of GST/HST; and (iv) hybrid mismatch and anti-avoidance rules in sections 18.4 and 18.5 of the Income Tax Act, which constrain deductions in cross-border arrangements involving inconsistent entity classification between Canada and another jurisdiction such as the United States.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST); in Alberta the provincial component is nil, so the applicable indirect tax is the federal 5% GST, imposed under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD — a person generally becomes required to register for GST/HST when taxable supplies, including worldwide taxable supplies, exceed $30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; a non-resident corporation carrying on a taxable supply business in Canada should assess its Canadian GST/HST nexus separately and may be required to register despite an absence of provincial sales tax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time e-invoicing or fiscal clearance regime. The CRA does not operate a digital stamping platform, and invoices may be issued in paper, PDF, or standard electronic formats, provided they contain the prescribed GST/HST invoice information: supplier name, Business Number or GST/HST registration number, date of invoice, description of supply, consideration, and the amount of GST/HST charged or a clear statement that the supply is tax-inclusive. Registrants with annual taxable revenue exceeding $1 million CAD are required to file GST/HST returns electronically using CRA GST/HST NETFILE or a registered EDI service.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply may be zero-rated under Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act if it qualifies as an export of tangible personal property or as a service supplied to a non-resident person. For an overseas public relations and communications firm, services supplied to non-resident clients, such as international media relations and crisis communications consulting, are generally eligible for zero-rating where the supply is made to a person who is not resident in Canada, the service is not supplied to an individual present in Canada at the time the service is performed, and the service is not performed in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada. The registrant must retain contemporaneous evidence demonstrating the non-resident status of the customer and the actual provision of the service, including the contract, service scope, power point of performance, and delivery of media or communications deliverables outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) for goods exported from Canada, or the underlying service contract, engagement letter, and detailed final invoice evidencing the supply to a non-resident client for the PR and communications services
Bill of Lading or air waybill for goods, or equivalent electronic delivery records and proof of service performance outside Canada for services
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT payment confirmation, bank credit advice, or ACH/Wire transfer evidence demonstrating actual receipt of payment from the non-resident client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA applies heightened audit scrutiny to zero-rated export transactions under GST/HST Memorandum 4-4-13. If the statutory documentary evidence is not maintained or the non-resident supply characterization is not substantiated at the time of audit, the CRA may reassess the supply as taxable at 5%, reverse input tax credits, impose arrears interest, and apply penalties. False statements or omission of material information attract penalties under section 280.1 of the Excise Tax Act, generally equal to the greater of C$250 and 25% of the net tax assessed or the refund claimed. Wilful evasion or gross negligence may lead to prosecution, additional fines of up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded, and criminal sanctions. Retrospective clawbbacks are possible because the CRA may reassess beyond the normal four-year limitation period where a registrant has made a misrepresentation, contrived a false export transaction, or failed to maintain adequate books and records.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); prudential regulation of deposit-taking institutions by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/CFT supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); payments infrastructure operated by Payments Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII obligations. No Foreign Exchange Control Act, no exchange licensing regime, and no prior regulatory approval applies to inbound capital injections, profit repatriation (dividends, interest, royalties, management fees), or loan servicing. Dividends and other outbound payments are subject solely to Part XIII Canadian withholding tax (default 25%, treaty-reduced to 5%/15% under the Canada-US and other tax treaties) and to applicable transfer-pricing/arm's-length documentation. No minimum holding period, no repatriation permit, and no net open position requirement is imposed on corporations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. A resident exporter may retain foreign currency receipts in Canadian-dollar or foreign-currency bank accounts, convert them freely, or use them for offshore operating disbursements. The only quantitative reporting obligation is statistical: direct investment and balance-of-payments transactions above threshold must be reported to Statistics Canada (via the International Transactions Reporting System, BERD, and Direct Investment forms), but these reports entail no surrender, conversion, or prior-approval duty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
ATB Financial (Provincial Crown Corporation of Alberta)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low for offshore digital EMIs. A foreign electronic money institution (EMI) may lawfully service a Canadian corporate client only if it registers as a money service business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) framework, registers as a retail payment service provider with the Bank of Canada. In practice, EMIs such as Wise or Airwallex can be used as supplementary low-value collection or disbursement conduits, but they commonly rely on Canadian chartered-bank sponsorship and may impose material balance caps, velocity limits, and narrower transaction-purpose tolerance. For a capital escrow and FX execution mandate, a Schedule I chartered-bank primary account remains the only fully reliable clearing and treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence or a live, secure video-verified interview is required for at least one authorized signing officer or director with Canadian nexus; remote-only onboarding is not generally available for non-resident-controlled corporations. Non-resident directors without prior Canadian banking history are typically required to attend a branch or embassy/consulate appointment, or to submit notarized/certified identity documents plus a banker's reference, before account activation. Alberta-registered corporations, being provincial entities, attract enhanced beneficial-ownership scrutiny, and banks may additionally demand proof of the physical office or substance in Alberta.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) with ≥25% interest, especially if located in a jurisdiction of concern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport and second identity documents; two independent proof-of-address documents; current Alberta corporate search certificate; organizational chart; formal register of ultimate beneficial owners; sworn declaration of source of wealth; banker's unconditional reference from the UBO's home-country financial institution; and a Canadian legal opinion confirming the clear title to contributed funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial paid-up capital injected by third-country or opaque funding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entire capital-structure chart (entity-by-entity); bank statements evidencing the exact source of funds; corporate board resolutions ratifying the injection; audited financial statements of the investing entity or an accountant's letter; and an opinion from Canadian counsel confirming that the funds are free of any criminal proceeds and not subject to foreign exchange or asset-freeze restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PR/communications business with undisclosed clients, passive fee flows, or unexplained high-volume retainer invoicing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client service agreements; verified client list (redacted where necessary); invoicing and expected payment schedule; sanctions/PEP screening reports; FINTRAC-compliant record of business relationships and transaction-monitoring policy; and a designated compliance officer appointment under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from sanctioned, embargoed, or high-risk jurisdictions, or cross-border trade in media/crisis-management content
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Substantiation of genuine commercial activity (contracts, scoping documents, deliverables); end-user and counterparty due-diligence certificates; real-time sanctions and adverse-media screening output; internal AML policy, risk assessment, and training records; and any Canadian Global Affairs Canada permits or OFSI/DFATD clearances where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital injections are routed by SWIFT MT103/MT202 via the remitting bank's correspondent into the Alberta operating account at a Canadian Schedule I bank. No Bank of Canada or OSFI approval is required; the remittance information field (MT103 /70) must clearly state 'capital contribution' or 'shareholder loan' for audit trail integrity. For equity contributions the bank may request a board resolution and the escrow ledger reconciliation; for shareholder loans, a signed loan agreement and interest terms are expected to satisfy transfer-pricing substance. If the injection constitutes inward foreign direct investment exceeding the Statistics Canada reporting threshold, a Direct Investment Report or BERD return must be filed; otherwise the transaction proceeds without prior authorization or conversion requirement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Canadian-dollar trade settlements and retainer fees clear via Payments Canada retail and high-value rails: the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for EFT/ACH batches and the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) for high-value real-time gross settlement. Cross-border USD, EUR, and GBP disbursements execute via SWIFT MT103 messages through the sponsoring bank's correspondent network (Fedwire/CHIPS for USD, T2 for EUR, CHAPS for GBP). Larger procurement or production settlements may be structured with commercial letters of credit issued in accordance with ICC UCP 600 and settled against documentary compliance; bank payment obligations and supply-chain finance facilities further optimize working capital. Real-time rail migration to the Real-Time Rail (RTR) is monitored but does not alter SWIFT/MT103 trade-clearing requirements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards between CAD and USD, EUR, GBP, and other freely convertible currencies, executed ISDA/CSA-documented with Schedule I bank counterparties (typically 1–12 month tenors).
Vanilla FX options, call/put spreads, and zero-cost collars determined by the treasury hedging policy, with board-approved delegation and no speculative uncovered positions.
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/GBP) under ISDA Master Agreements, used to convert fixed or floating interest liabilities without disturbing the underlying trade payables.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market or restricted currencies where CAD deliverability is unavailable; NDFs are not used for CAD/USD or other G7 pairs because full deliverability exists.

Currency swaps with settlement against trade-clearing banks under collateralized CSA arrangements, limited to underlying retainer and production-cycle exposures verified by forecast cash-flow statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Form AR-01, Alberta Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta, Corporate Registry System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after each fiscal year end (anniversary-based; e.g., December 31 FYE due by March 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty C$50 after the 90-day deadline; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution under s. 212 ABCA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal corporate filing with provincial allocation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Corporate Taxation Directorate / Calgary Tax Services Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end (e.g., June 30 for December 31 year-end); balance-due day is three months after year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 5% of balance due plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months for late filings; 10%-50% gross negligence penalty; repeated failure under s. 162(2) can attract administrative penalties up to C$25,000 and criminal prosecution for wilful omission

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (IBO register review concurrent with annual return cycle)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (confirmation retained in corporate records; not publicly filed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the Alberta Annual Return, no later than 90 days after fiscal year end; directors must confirm IBO details remain accurate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with Alberta Business Corporations Act beneficial ownership transparency rules: fines up to C$200,000 and/or 6 months' imprisonment for false or omitted information; continued violation permits court-ordered compliance and potential administrative dissolution

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit for a non-distributing Alberta private corporation with fewer than 16 shareholders per s. 151(1) ABCA; independent auditor required only when the corporation is a 'distributing corporation' (public or prescribed) or is requisitioned by shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public accountable enterprises; otherwise Canadian GAAP options under CPA Canada Handbook — Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) or IFRS for SMEs; tax return compiled on CRA accounting basis from fiscal net income

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act (Beneficial Ownership Transparency amendments), directors must take reasonable steps to identify individual beneficial owners holding 25% or more of shares or exercising control over the corporation, and record them in the internal IBO register maintained at the registered office; an annual confirmation is performed on each annual return date to verify accuracy, and any change in beneficial ownership must be recorded within 30 days of discovery
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individual Beneficial Owners (IBO Register)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$250-$550 per year for Alberta registered office and registered agent compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$3,500-$8,500 for a small private corporation full audit; US$1,200-$2,500 for review engagement alternative

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% on the first $500,000 of active business income (small business rate); 38% on passive income and active business income exceeding $500,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) tax credits and deductions; no provincial incentives in Alberta

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically through CRA's My Business Account
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end (e.g. March 31 for calendar year corporations)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident corporations, report only Canadian-source income; non-residents do not file T2 but may receive NR4 for withholding
Sum of gross income minus deductions; non-residents limited to Canadian source
Taxable income after deductions; non-residents file if having Canadian source income
Calculated at 15% small business or 38% general rate; non-residents pay on Canadian source only

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $100 per day to a maximum of $2,500; failure to pay tax on time incurs interest at prescribed rates; substantial understatement penalties up to 50% of tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% federal withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, subject to reduction under applicable income tax treaties
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a valid tax treaty certificate from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); the corporation withholds tax at the reduced treaty rate and issues a T4 summary to the non-resident; file NR4 with CRA by March 31
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% federal rate, reduced to 0-10% under most tax treaties; Interest: 25% federal rate, reduced to 0-10% under tax treaties (e.g. 0% under Canada-US treaty for certain interest)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: $500,000 CAD for local file documentation; $50 million CAD for master file documentation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations do not apply in Canada; however, General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and transfer pricing rules require transactions to have economic substance and arm's length pricing

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate misrepresentation or omission of income or expenses to reduce tax payable
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction; fines up to $1,000,000; imprisonment up to 5 years; restitution orders
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for willful evasion; potential criminal charges, fines, and disqualification from office

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Late Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission or late submission of T2 return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of $100 per day, capped at $2,500; additional penalties for continued default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: No direct personal liability for filing, but directors may face personal liability for unpaid source deductions or other taxes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or file transfer pricing documentation or using non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10-50% of the transfer pricing adjustment; possible reassessment and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable if they directed or acquiesced in the non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold and remit WHT on dividends paid to non-residents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty equal to the amount of tax not remitted; interest on unpaid tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties if they failed to comply with remittance obligations
